sense.def: The Ancient Roman Monarchy (traditionally 753–509 BCE): the regal period of the city-state on the Tiber, from its legendary founder Romulus to the expulsion of Tarquinius Superbus, during which the king combined military command with sacral functions.

The Roman Empire (27 BCE–476 CE in the West, until 1453 CE in the East): the monarchical regime founded by Augustus on the ruins of the Republic, ruled by an emperor who was at once supreme military commander and pontifex maximus, and whose eastern half survived as the Byzantine Empire.

The Latin Roman Church (Catholic): the Western Christian Church centred on the See of Rome and headed by the Pope, heir to the city's religious and administrative prestige after the fall of the Western Empire.
